- **self**: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds (8/2)

## How it works

- [statement] In MongoDB 7.1 and later, fixed-bucket query optimizations require a collection created with both custom parameters and no later parameter changes. For eligible predicates using $gte and $lt on the timeField, MongoDB can omit the per-measurement event filter when the query bounds align with bucket boundaries. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The time-span setting is only one bucket constraint. MongoDB documents a maximum of 1,000 measurements or 125 KB per bucket, whichever is lower, so a configured maximum time span does not guarantee that a bucket remains open for that entire interval. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md, https://ds02.haw.tuhh.de/bitstream/20.500.12738/18748/1/BA_Szenarienbasierte_Evaluation_von_Zeitreihen-Datenbanksystemen.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] During insertion, the BucketCatalog closes an open bucket if the incoming measurement would make the time between the bucket's oldest and newest timestamps exceed the collection's allowed span. A bucket closed for this reason remains eligible for reopening. bucketRoundingSeconds positions a new bucket's lower time boundary; it is not the span limit. (high confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md, https://www.doctrine-project.org/projects/doctrine-mongodb-odm/en/2.14/reference/attributes-reference.html
- [statement] After collection creation, collMod can increase granularity or the custom span and rounding values but cannot decrease them. Existing bucket documents are not rewritten when the setting changes; the new span applies to new buckets. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-limitations.md · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/collMod.md, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/query/timeseries/README.md, https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md
- [statement] An October 2023 forum report describes MongoDB 7.0.2 rejecting a 300-second custom pair after an upgrade from 6.0.3 with the error that bucketMaxSpanSeconds was not configurable away from the default 3,600 for the provided granularity. A MongoDB respondent attributed the failure to an incomplete upgrade and advised following the release procedure; this is version-specific troubleshooting evidence. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-10-09) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/problem-setting-bucketmaxspanseconds-and-bucketroundingseconds-in-mongodb-timeseries-collection/248318 · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] MongoDB 6.3 and later supports manual fixed-window bucketing with bucketMaxSpanSeconds and bucketRoundingSeconds instead of granularity. The two values must be equal, between 1 and 31,536,000 seconds inclusive, and granularity must be omitted. bucketMaxSpanSeconds limits the oldest-to-newest time range in a bucket. When a new bucket is opened, bucketRoundingSeconds rounds the first measurement's timestamp down to determine the bucket's minimum time. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md, https://prisma.github.io/prisma-engines/doc/src/mongodb/db/options.rs.html, https://www.doctrine-project.org/projects/doctrine-mongodb-odm/en/2.14/reference/attributes-reference.html, https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MongoDB describes granularity as the expected cadence between measurements. Its presets map to bucketRoundingSeconds and bucketMaxSpanSeconds as follows: seconds = 60 and 3,600; minutes = 3,600 and 86,400; hours = 86,400 and 2,592,000. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo/blob/master/src/mongo/db/timeseries/README.md, https://www.doctrine-project.org/projects/doctrine-mongodb-odm/en/2.14/reference/attributes-reference.html, https://pkg.go.dev/go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/mongo/options
- [statement] In a September 2024 migration discussion, one user reported that custom 3,600-second bucketing made queries slower and the collection larger than using granularity: hours. This is a workload-specific report, not a general benchmark or a contradiction of the fixed-boundary rules. (low confidence) (verified as of 2024-09-04) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/migration-to-timeseries-collection/295416 · keywords: Time series bucketing parameters: granularity, bucketMaxSpanSeconds, bucketRoundingSeconds · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-granularity.md
